items.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I admired him so greatly for that. I’ve studied his early records with that small group

ctx.x: We’ve been talking about getting people’s opinion on the Count Basie Orchestra, Basie as a musician and also Joe Williams.

Oh, you’re talking about some favorite subjects of mine. Well I think, you know there’s no doubt that Joe Williams and Count Basie changed the public’s concept of jazz I think, because Count Basie was a very engaging piano player. Now this was not always so. When he played with just small groups, he played like any hot jazz pianist, you know. The style that he used with his big band was altogether different, and they were both wonderful. But if he had, he was wise enough, let me put it that way, that he knew the…
I think from what he told us he had played them together at the same time.
